Precondition: A shop-floor action available (e.g. move or split a LOT)
Step: Perform the action then open the LOT's history detail
Expected Result: An Audit.OperationLog entry is written with timestamp, user, terminal, location, severity, event type, entity type, entity id, and description
Notes: No standalone operation-log browser; witnessed via LOT history detail / DB inspection

Precondition: A mutating proc that fails after opening its transaction
Step: Trigger a mutation that rolls back
Expected Result: The operation-log write is atomic with the mutation — a rolled-back mutation leaves no orphan log row (write occurs inside the proc transaction)

Precondition: Config Tool Audit (Config Log) browser reachable at /audit
Step: Open the browser and apply Entity Type / Severity / date-range / search filters
Expected Result: The Configuration Log lists config changes; Apply filters and Reset clears them; timestamps display in Eastern time

Step: Make an engineering change (e.g. deprecate a downtime reason code), then find it in the Config Log and open its detail
Expected Result: Entry shows the change with a structured old/new JSON diff carrying resolved-name FK sub-objects; detail popup renders the change

Precondition: An external call path available (AIM or Zebra print)
Step: Trigger the external call and inspect Audit.InterfaceLog
Expected Result: An interface-log row is written with system name, direction (INBOUND/OUTBOUND), event type, and description
Notes: No dedicated interface-log browser; witness by DB inspection

Step: Cause a rejected mutation (e.g. deprecate an entity with active dependents), then open the Failure Log
Expected Result: Entry shows the attempted timestamp, user, entity, event type, failure reason, procedure name, and a JSON snapshot of the input parameters; detail popup opens

Precondition: Failure Log browser open with several logged rejections
Expected Result: Top Rejection Reasons and Top Failing Procedures tiles aggregate the rejections; entity/user/procedure/date filters narrow the list

Step: Enable high-fidelity mode for one target system
Expected Result: Full RequestPayload and ResponsePayload are stored for that system; the mode is toggleable per target system without a restart

Precondition: Any audit browser with an Event Type facet
Step: Inspect the event type values on log entries
Expected Result: Event types come from the normalized LogEventType table (e.g. LotMoved, DowntimeStarted, ConfigChanged) with no free-text drift; an unseeded code cannot be written

Step: Open the Entity Type filter dropdown
Expected Result: Entity types are populated from the normalized LogEntityType table (Lot, DowntimeEvent, DowntimeReasonCode, Location, etc.)

Precondition: Access to a shared audit proc call path
Step: Confirm the shared audit procs accept code strings and reject an unresolvable one
Expected Result: Shared audit procs accept event/entity/severity as code strings resolved to ids internally; a code that does not resolve raises an error (surfaces a seeding gap/typo)

Step: Inspect proc signatures and result-set behavior
Expected Result: Procs return exactly one result set and declare no OUTPUT parameters; mutations emit a single SELECT Status/Message/NewId and reads return an empty set for not-found
